claim: Visceral Pedagogy: 'You'll never forget how a compressor works after pumping blood through arteries' — the grotesque is mandatory pedagogy; and The Neural Network Synthesis Paradigm: inhibition makes rhythm as negative space.

pieces.what: One compressor, two faces: a plain gain-reduction meter with threshold/ratio/attack/release, and the same arithmetic as a heart and arteries (pressure = amplitude, vessel diameter = gain reduction, pulse rate = attack), on the same signal. A stated test of whether the metaphor changes what a user sets — a task given twice, the settings compared, chance level and rule first; the pedagogy claim itself is a memory claim no piece can test, and the piece says so.
pieces.walks_up_from: the plain meter alone on a steady tone

pieces.what: A small inhibitory network: a steady trigger drives a few nodes, inhibitory links suppress competitors, and a rhythm appears in the gaps; the test removes the inhibition and measures what the rhythm loses (inter-onset interval entropy, syncopation against the trigger grid), so 'rhythm as negative space' can fail.
pieces.walks_up_from: one neuron firing on every trigger
